interface.name: inox_ipc
interface.description:
Private, unstable Inox protocol used for control messages between the compositor and the Inox shell and session components.
This protocol is an Inox extension and is not part of the upstream wayland-protocols. It is versioned independently and its interface may change in a backwards-incompatible way until Inox 1.0; consumers must negotiate via the version event instead of assuming a fixed revision.
The global is advertised by the compositor. A client binds it once and uses it to ask the compositor to perform session-wide control actions.
Version 2 adds the trusted session-lock role: a client claims it with claim_lock_role before the compositor will accept a session lock from it, and the compositor reports whether the session is currently locked through the session_lock_state event so that observers such as the idle daemon and the notification daemon do not have to infer it. The event is a notification from the authority, never a capability: any binding client may observe it, and none gains a permission from it.

description.summary: whether the compositor currently holds the session lock

entry.name: locked
entry.summary: the session is locked and every output is covered

entry.name: rejected
entry.summary: the request was rejected by the compositor

entry.name: io_error
entry.summary: reading or writing persistent state failed

entry.name: unsupported
entry.summary: the requested operation is not supported

request.name: get_version

description.summary: ask the compositor to report the inox-ipc protocol version

request.description: Ask the compositor to send the current version event. Clients use this to negotiate capabilities before issuing other requests.

request.name: reload_config

description.summary: ask the compositor to reload its configuration from disk

request.description: Ask the compositor to re-read its configuration and apply it atomically. The compositor answers with a config_reloaded event. On failure the compositor must keep the previously active configuration.

request.name: claim_lock_role

description.summary: claim the trusted session-lock role for this connection

request.description:
Claims the trusted session-lock role for the connection this object belongs to. The compositor only accepts a session lock request from a connection that has claimed the role with the token the session delivered to the trusted lock client; a claim with a missing, wrong or already-used token leaves the connection unauthorized.
Authorization is bound to the connection and its lifetime, not to a client-supplied name, process id or application id: those are claims by the client and are not evidence. A connection that never claims the role is refused the lock with the finished event, which the ext-session-lock-v1 protocol defines for exactly this case. A compositor that has no token configured refuses every claim.

arg.name: token
arg.summary: one-shot token delivered by the session

description.summary: the inox-ipc protocol version implemented by the compositor

arg.name: version
arg.summary: protocol version implemented by the compositor

event.name: session_lock_state

description.summary: the session lock state, sent on bind and on every change

event.description:
Reports whether the compositor currently holds the session lock. It is sent once when the global is bound and again whenever the state changes, so a client never has to guess the initial state and never has to poll.
This is the authoritative statement of the compositor that owns the lock; it is not an authorization and carries no capability. It is what lets the idle daemon require a confirmed lock before a suspend and what lets the notification daemon withhold notification bodies while the session is locked.
